Round 2: the last 10 profiling slots, ranked after closure 2 (one checker on the unmerged profiler file)

Round 3: line check of the opening line and bottleneck guess of the 30 High and Medium plants profiled in rounds 1-2, by a checker who did not write them (plants profiled later were line-checked in their own rounds)
Round 4: the six base plants that entered the top 40 after the one-basis relationship ruling (consultation 31)
Round 5: Besser Pro Paris TX, the one base plant that entered the top 40 after the R3 lead verification
Cross-vertical checks (state air permits, job-board dates, OSHA headcounts, profiles of OSHA top-40 entrants): rows for this vertical's plants
Base-record sample: 25 base and 8 excluded records drawn with a fixed seed after closure 2 and both miss verifications (reported separately; not a profile round)

miss_rate.note: R2 blind audit after closure 2, on one population (consultation 32): every in-definition plant the two R2 auditors listed plus all 81 leads they left in their notes, each classified by hand. 20 verified misses / (91 included plants the auditors named + 20). Misses: 9 from the auditors' lists (10 confirmed minus SAF-Holland Dumas, a lead under T16), 6 from the 18 never-screened note leads, 5 from the 24 screen-only or held note leads. On the auditors' lists alone: 9/73 = 12.3%. On auditor C's local-source confirmed rows alone: 2/17 = 11.8%. Against the list before closure 2: 27/111 = 24.3%. Upper bound counting every not-confirmed candidate (28, mostly dead domains, sources from 2013-2017 or no current operating source) plus SAF Dumas and Tuff Ferndale: 50/141 = 35.5%. Neither auditor reached a dry point, and both drifted off-frame (C drew 15 of its 37 confirmed plants from trade press; D used the bulk NHTSA recall file). R1 measured 24.3%, restated to 22.5% after rulings T16-T17 were applied to found and missed plants alike.
history: 22.5% (R1 after rulings T16-T17, applied both ways)
12.3% (R2 auditor lists after closure 2; first logged as 11.1%, an arithmetic error)
18.0% (R2 with all 81 note leads classified and verified, 2026-11-20)

known_limits: Neither blind audit reached a dry point in either round; the R2 upper bound is 35.5% if every not-confirmed candidate were a real operating plant. Misses concentrate in small makers: of the 76 verified misses now in the ledger (both rounds), 31 have an OSHA 2025 row.

Rulings: T16-T18 were written after the R1 candidate names were known and before closure 2 and the R2 audit; T19-T21 were written after closure 2 returned, and T21 was refined after the R2 verification (consultation 31). Each was applied to found and missed plants alike.

Base records rest partly on registry footing (T15: an OSHA 336212 record plus an EPA name, prospect low confidence; T18: a government or association record naming the trailer type). Component, tank-trailer, stale and unshown-product sites (about 210 distinct lead rows) stay in the screen files, not on the map; the NATM directory sweep (closure TR-P) left 599 of its 841 rows screened with no site evidence, mostly small members nobody read in depth.

Profiled: 47 plants in five trailers rounds (30 + 10, then 6 and 1 that entered the top 40 after later rulings and misses) plus 4 multi-vertical plants profiled in other verticals; Hardin Lacon was fact-checked in the data-center rounds.
osha.gov is blocked from this session: OSHA headcounts rest on the 2025 national file under the gate rule; EPA FRS timed out for much of the day (ECHO used instead).
ADP Workforce Now job boards return about 20 requisitions per call; five boards were re-read with paging, the others were not, so a few postings may be missing from base records.
